# settle-mcp

An MCP server that explains SETTLE and KANERVA, sets them up on your machine, and runs them.

> The website is the source of truth. These docs are generated from the SETTLE site (its pages, its English strings, the SETTLE docs and the KANERVA README it shows) by `tools/build_mcp_docs.mjs`. Never edit a generated file by hand; change the site and rebuild.

Built on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.31.0, stdio transport. MIT licence.

## The three parts

### PART ONE · DOCS AND HELP

What everything is named and how it works. Needs nothing installed.

- `help`: Explain SETTLE, KANERVA and this server. With a topic, look the word up in the glossary built from the site and its docs; "glossary" lists every name.
- `read_doc`: Read one SETTLE, KANERVA or site document by name (for example "03-syntax", "sdm", "kanerva://readme", "what"); with no name, list them.
- `list_examples`: List the tested example programs from the SETTLE docs, each with its first comment line. Filter by family or by kind (ok or error).
- `get_example`: Show one tested example: its program and the exact output (or error) the interpreter is tested to produce.
- `explain_error`: Explain a SETTLE error message: the documented cause, where it is documented, and a tested program that produces it.

### PART TWO · SETUP

Check the machine, then fetch, build and verify SETTLE and KANERVA in a folder you choose.

- `check_system`: Check this machine for what SETTLE needs (rustc, cargo, git, node) by running only version commands. Shows each command it ran.
- `setup`: Fetch, build and verify SETTLE and KANERVA in a folder. Dry run by default: returns every command and a plan id. Run it with dry_run false and confirm set to that id.
- `setup_status`: Report a setup that is still running in the background, step by step, or the last setup this server ran.

### PART THREE · USAGE

Run SETTLE programs, store and recall with a sparse distributed memory, run KANERVA.

- `run_program`: Run a SETTLE program, from a .settle file or from program text, and return what it printed, its errors and its exit code.
- `sdm_store_recall`: Write named patterns (or short texts) into a sparse distributed memory, then read one back from a noisy read-address. Shows the SETTLE program it ran.
- `kanerva_quickstart`: Run the KANERVA crate's own quickstart example: build a memory, write 300 patterns, read one back, predict capacity, refuse, a keyed note and the soft machine.

## From scratch

### 1. Install Node

settle-mcp runs on Node 18 or newer. Check with `node --version`; if it is missing, install it from nodejs.org.

### 2. Get the package

Clone its repository, `github.com/triplesparkle/settle-mcp`. The repository is private for now, so a clone needs access; once it is public anyone can clone it or download its zip. Then install its two dependencies (the MCP SDK and zod):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/triplesparkle/settle-mcp
cd settle-mcp
npm install
node src/bin.js --version
```

### 3. Add it to Claude Code

One command adds it for your user:

```sh
claude mcp add settle -- node /path/to/settle-mcp/src/bin.js
```

### 4. Or add it to a project, Claude Desktop, or any MCP client

For a project, put this in `.mcp.json` at the project root. For Claude Desktop, put the same `mcpServers` block in `claude_desktop_config.json` (on macOS in `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/`, on Windows in `%APPDATA%\Claude\`) and restart it. Any client that speaks MCP over stdio takes the same command and arguments.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "settle": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/path/to/settle-mcp/src/bin.js"]
    }
  }
}
```

### 5. Ask for help

Ask the assistant to call `help`. It works with nothing installed: the three parts, every tool, and a glossary of every SETTLE and KANERVA name. Try `help` with the topic `lean`, `radius` or `glossary`.

### 6. Set SETTLE up

Call `check_system`, then `setup` with a `folder` and a `settle_source`: the local folder holding `settle-rs`, or a git URL you were given. The first call is a dry run that lists every command and returns a plan id. Read it, then call `setup` again with `dry_run` false and `confirm` set to that id.

```json
{ "folder": "~/settle", "settle_source": "/path/to/settle-rs" }
```

### 7. Run a first program

Call `list_examples`, pick one, and call `run_program` with its path, or pass program text as `source`:

```json
{ "source": "model :m do\n  thing :rain, leans: :no, by: 1\nend\nrun :m do\n  settle 2_000, seed: 1\n  ask :rain\nend\n" }
```

### 8. Store and recall a memory

Call `sdm_store_recall` with a few names, one of them holding a short text, and read that one back from a noisy read-address:

```json
{ "patterns": [{ "name": "cat" }, { "name": "dog" }, { "name": "note", "text": "meet at nine" }], "read": "note", "noise": 0.15 }
```
